title: Licensing and launch approval for space nuclear reactors
bottleneck: Launching a nuclear reactor — even one staying inert until orbit — requires interagency approval spanning NASA, DOE, the NRC, and the White House, plus National Environmental Policy Act review and launch-safety analysis proving no credible accident disperses radioactive material. The process is slow, expensive, and politically sensitive, shaped by decades of anti-nuclear sentiment. DRACO faces exactly this gauntlet, and each new reactor design largely restarts it.
why_it_blocks: Technical readiness is meaningless if a reactor cannot legally launch; the regulatory timeline can exceed the engineering timeline, killing programs before hardware flies.
current_state: Updated presidential directives streamlined some approvals, and DRACO is working through the process toward a 2027 demo. No general fast-track licensing framework for commercial space reactors exists.
